answers.answer: Leave 4 tokens of each of the five gem colors and all 5 gold tokens. Reveal 3 nobles; remove all unrevealed nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Setup: 2 players: 4 gems per color, 5 gold, 3 nobles; "Remove remaining noble tiles from the game".

answers.answer: For 3 players use 5 gems per color, 5 gold and 4 nobles. For 4 players use 7 gems per color, 5 gold and 5 nobles: two more of each gem color, the same gold count and one more noble.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count: 3 | 5 | 5 | 4; 4 | 7 | 5 | 5.

answers.answer: Shuffle each level deck separately. Put them in a central column with level 1 at the bottom, level 2 in the middle and level 3 at the top. Reveal 4 cards per level, 12 total in a 3-by-4 grid. The youngest player starts and play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player: "The youngest player goes first. Play proceeds clockwise."

answers.answer: Choose exactly one action: take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different colors; take 2 non-gold gems of one color only if that pile has at least 4 before taking; reserve 1 face-up market card or the top card of a level deck only while holding fewer than 3 reserved cards, taking 1 gold if available; or purchase 1 face-up market card or a card reserved on a previous turn by paying its cost after bonuses, with gold allowed as a substitute. You cannot take gems and buy on the same turn, or reserve and buy that card on that same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "must perform exactly one"; purchase "1 card you reserved on a previous turn"; Reserve a Development Card gives both sources.

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times, including their colors and quantities as represented by the visible tokens.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times."

answers.answer: You may take 2 green, leaving 2, because there are 4 before taking. You may not take 2 red from a pile of 3. Check the threshold before taking the tokens. Neither the 3-different-color action nor the 2-same-color action can take gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: "at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them"; both gem-taking actions specify "no gold".

answers.answer: Temporarily holding 12 is allowed. Return 2 tokens of your choice to reach exactly 10 by the end of the turn; they can include gems just drawn. Gold counts toward the 10-token limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: "may temporarily exceed 10"; "return tokens of their choice"; "including gold"; "some or all of the tokens they just took".

answers.answer: Reserve the card and take 1 gold, temporarily reaching 11 tokens; return 1 token of your choice, potentially that gold, to finish with 10. If the gold supply is empty, still reserve the card, take no gold and remain at 10 tokens.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: "If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve"; Token Hand Limit permits returning gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve either 1 face-up card from the market or the top card of any one of the three level decks. A card taken from a deck is not shown to opponents. Only the player who reserved a card can purchase it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: "face-up" or "top card"; "without revealing it"; "only ... the player who reserved them".

answers.answer: You cannot reserve a fourth card, including merely to obtain gold. You cannot discard a reserved card or exchange one to make room; the only way a reserved card leaves your hand is by purchasing it.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: "If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another"; "only way ... is to purchase it".

answers.answer: Immediately refill the reserved face-up level-2 card’s space with the top card of the level-2 deck. Purchasing any face-up card similarly causes immediate replacement from its matching level deck. Buying a reserved card removes it from your hand and creates no market vacancy or refill. If the relevant deck is empty, the vacated market space stays empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: "Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved ... immediately replaced"; "If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty".

answers.answer: Spend 1 green token; the 2 blue bonuses cover both blue costs. If bonuses cover all required colors and quantities, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Purchase payment example: "2 blue bonuses ... only need to spend 1 green token"; "without spending any tokens at all"; bonuses are permanent.

answers.answer: Yes. After bonuses, the unpaid cost is 1 blue, 1 black and 1 white. Pay the blue token for blue and one gold each for black and white. Return all three spent tokens to the supply. Keep all bonus cards; their discounts are permanent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce costs; "Gold tokens ... substitute for any single gem token"; spent gems and gold return to supply; permanent bonuses.

answers.answer: Purchase 1 face-up card from the market or 1 previously reserved card from your own hand, paying its cost after bonuses, using gems and/or gold as needed. Place purchased cards face up in front of you, grouped by bonus color and staggered so all bonuses and prestige values remain visible to everyone at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card; "sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible ... at all times".

answers.answer: You do not qualify with only 2 white bonuses: a white token or gold cannot substitute for the missing bonus. Acquiring a third white bonus makes you qualify at the end of your turn, provided the noble remains available. Bonuses above the requirement do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "at least" the required bonuses; "bonuses only ... not gem tokens".

answers.answer: Choose 1 noble; you cannot take both or decline all. The visit is automatic and uses no extra action. It gives 3 prestige. Eligibility is checked at the end of your turn, after the action and token-limit check; at most 1 noble is received per turn.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: "cannot refuse"; "not an action"; "choose one"; "3 prestige points"; Turn Structure orders token limit before noble check.

answers.answer: Place the received noble tile face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: "Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you."

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns; A does not take another turn. This completes the round with equal turn counts. B is not guaranteed to win: the most prestige at the end wins, so another player can surpass B.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: complete current round for "same number of turns"; End-of-Game Clarifications: triggering player may not win.

answers.answer: Your total becomes 16. Reaching 15 or more triggers the end even when you pass over 15. Complete the current round to give everyone equal turns, then determine the winner by total prestige, using the purchased-development tiebreaker if needed.
answers.evidence: Nobles are worth 3; End-Game Trigger: "15 or more"; Determining the Winner and Tiebreaker.

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie at 16, and B has only 9 purchased developments versus A’s 10. C’s 15 cannot win regardless of C’s fewer cards. Nobles count toward prestige. B’s 3 unpurchased reserved cards do not count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: most prestige; "Noble tile points count"; Tiebreaker: "fewest development cards" purchased.

answers.answer: No. The 8 printed prestige on unpurchased reserved cards count neither toward your score nor the 15-point trigger. Their 2 white bonuses do not reduce purchase costs or qualify for nobles until those cards are purchased.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: "Printed on each purchased card"; payment bonuses come from "previously purchased development cards"; nobles use bonuses "from purchased development cards".

answers.answer: You receive no physical blue token. The purchased card supplies a permanent blue discount for future purchases and a blue bonus toward noble requirements even though its prestige value is zero.
answers.evidence: Development Cards: prestige "may be 0"; Bonus Stacking: "never generate tokens"; each purchased card adds one permanent bonus; nobles require purchased-card bonuses.

answers.answer: The card’s own blue bonus cannot make its purchase free: only previously purchased cards discount the cost, so without blue payment or gold you cannot buy it. A newly purchased white-bonus card does count for a noble checked at the end of this same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "bonuses from previously purchased development cards"; purchased cards add permanent bonuses; noble check occurs after the action at turn end.

answers.answer: The 3 excess blue bonuses cannot cover green or create blue change. You still owe 2 green tokens, with gold able to substitute for either or both. No blue token payment is needed.
answers.evidence: Bonuses reduce costs of their color; Bonus Stacking: excess "provides no benefit ... (no change is given)"; gold substitutes for any gem.

answers.answer: The first noble does not consume your permanent bonuses. If the other noble remains available, taking 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different available colors, or 2 non-gold gems of one color with at least 4 in its supply before taking, can still be followed by receiving that noble at the end of your next turn. You cannot collect it during an opponent’s turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses are permanent; nobles check "at the end of their turn"; other qualifying nobles "remain available for future turns".

answers.answer: Yes. With no reserved cards you may reserve that face-up level-3 card regardless of affordability. Reserving takes the card into your hand without paying its printed purchase cost, and you take 1 gold if available. Immediately refill its market space from that level’s deck if possible.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: take a face-up card into hand and "also take 1 gold"; only reserved-card limit stated; paying cost belongs to Purchase a Development Card.

answers.answer: No market card is removed or refilled: you took the top card directly from the level-2 deck. All 12 face-up market cards remain. You take only 1 reserved card, with no second replacement card for your hand; take 1 gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card offers face-up or top-of-deck reservation; Turn Structure: "Reserve 1 development card"; replacement is for face-up market acquisitions.

answers.answer: The 4 face-up cards remain available for purchase or reservation. Buying 1 leaves its space empty permanently because the deck is empty. The other 3 face-up cards remain available.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: "If the corresponding deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty"; market retains cards unless acquired; purchase and reservation allow face-up cards.

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy 1 affordable card previously reserved in their own hand, paying its cost after bonuses with gems or gold, or instead take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different available color piles. Only one action is allowed on that turn.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: exhaustion "does not end the game"; continue remaining legal actions "including purchasing reserved cards"; Turn Structure lists gem action.

answers.answer: Yes. Take 1 non-gold gem from each of the 3 different available colors, temporarily reaching 13 tokens, then return all 3 newly taken tokens to finish at 10 with the same holdings. A net gain is not required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: temporary excess permitted; "may return some or all of the tokens they just took".

answers.answer: A’s 2 spent gold return to the supply. B may reserve 1 card while holding fewer than 3 reserved cards and take 1 of that gold. Immediately after B takes it, before any token-limit returns, 1 gold remains in the supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply"; reserving takes "1 gold token" if available.

answers.answer: Yes. You may purchase the face-up level-3 card now if you can pay its cost after bonuses. The summary allows a face-up development purchase without requiring lower-level cards first.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card: "Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost"; no level prerequisite in the listed conditions.

answers.answer: You cannot skip an eligible noble visit. The purchase raises you from 12 to 15, then the automatic noble adds 3 for a total of 18. Other players whose turns remain in the current round continue, so everyone finishes with equal turn counts.
answers.evidence: Noble visit "automatic ... cannot refuse"; noble value 3; "15 or more" completes the current round.

answers.answer: The game ends after D completes this turn. A does not start another round, and nobody receives an extra turn: A, B, C and D have already taken equal numbers of turns when D finishes the current round.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: "the current round is completed so that every player has played the same number of turns".

answers.answer: Do not replace the noble from the 7 removed tiles; those tiles are permanently out of the game. Put the acquired noble face up in front of its recipient. There are now 2 available nobles in the middle.
answers.evidence: Setup removes remaining nobles; Noble Tile Mechanics: "out of the game permanently"; Noble Visits: place acquired tile face up in front of you.

answers.answer: Emerald is green; diamond is white; sapphire is blue; onyx is black; ruby is red; gold joker is yellow. There are 90 development cards: 40 level 1, 30 level 2 and 20 level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token-color table and Development Cards table: 40, 30, 20; 90 total.

answers.answer: You may spend 1 gold instead of the green and keep your green token. Gold can substitute for any single gem token; the summary imposes no requirement to spend an available matching gem first. Return the spent gold to the supply.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: "Gold tokens ... can substitute for any single gem token"; "Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply".

answers.answer: Yes. Take 1 red, 1 blue and 1 green. The 4-token minimum applies only to taking 2 of the same color. The piles then contain 0 red, 1 blue and 2 green.
answers.evidence: Take 3 Gem Tokens of Different Colors: "Take 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles"; 4-token requirement appears under Take 2 ... Same Color.

answers.answer: Directly exchanging gold for a red token is not one of the four listed actions and is not a use authorized by the stated joker rule. Gold substitutes for 1 gem token of any color when paying to purchase a development; spent gold goes back to the supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists exactly four actions; Gold Token Specifics: "substitute for any gem color when purchasing a card".

answers.answer: You must choose exactly 1 legal action and cannot voluntarily pass. Options are: take 1 non-gold token from each of 3 different available gem colors; take 2 non-gold tokens of one color only with at least 4 in that pile before taking; reserve 1 market card or top card of a level deck only with fewer than 3 cards reserved and take 1 gold if available; or purchase 1 face-up market card or 1 previously reserved card from your own hand by paying its cost after bonuses, with gold substitutes permitted.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: a player "must perform exactly one" of the four listed actions; reservation sources and payment conditions in Actions.

answers.answer: Sort gem and gold tokens by color into 6 distinct piles, placing them within reach of all players.
answers.evidence: Setup step 5: "in 6 distinct piles sorted by color, within reach of all players".

answers.answer: Your final prestige score is 15: 12 from purchased developments plus 3 from the acquired noble. The 4 unspent gold and 5 other gems add no prestige.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources lists purchased-card printed points and noble tiles at 3 each; no token points are listed.
